title: Some Protestants make forensic sense perpetual; most allow real change
source_text: VI. Porro hanc perpetuam esse vocis justificandi in Scriptura sacra significationem, neque unquam illa designari realem immutationem, per quam aliquis ex impio justus sanctusque efficitur, affirmant quidam inter Protestantes. Sed plerique aliter sentiunt, & meo quidem judicio, magna cum ratione. Nam verbum istud in aliquot Scripturae locis non, nisi dure & coacte admodum, potest admittere sensum illum forensem, neque justificari significat solum justum declarari, vel pronunciari, sed revera pium justumque fieri. Talis est omnium fere judicio locus qui habetur apud Danielem, cap. 12. Qui docti fuerint fulgebunt quasi splendor firmamenti; & qui justificant multos, quasi stellae in perpetuas aeternitates. Ubi per eos qui multos justificant, non intelliguntur illi qui multos justos habent, sive declarant, sed, ut habet versio Vulgata, qui ad justitiam erudiunt multos; aut, ut vertit nostra vernacula, qui ad justitiam multos introducunt: adeo ut justificare idem ibi sit quod justum reddere doctrina & exemplo vitae.
pass_a_gloss: Further, that this is the perpetual signification of the word justifying in sacred Scripture, and that by it a real change is never designated, by which someone is made just and holy out of an impious man, certain among the Protestants affirm. But most think otherwise, and in my judgment with great reason. For that word in some places of Scripture cannot admit that forensic sense except harshly and forcedly, nor does to be justified signify only to be declared or pronounced just, but truly to be made pious and just. Such in nearly everyone's judgment is the place in Daniel 12: They that are learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that justify many, as stars unto perpetual eternities. Where by those who justify many are not understood those who hold or declare many just, but, as the Vulgate has it, who instruct many unto righteousness; or, as our vernacular renders, who bring many in unto righteousness: so that to justify there is the same as to render just by teaching and by the example of life.
pass_b_english: Some Protestants claim forensic sense is perpetual and never means real change.
Most (and Le Blanc) disagree: Dan 12 justify many = instruct unto righteousness.

choices.why: Here causative teaching, not mere verdict.
